## .NET 8 → .NET 9 Breaking Changes & Fixes

### 1. TFM update (WebApi.csproj)
`net8.0` → `net9.0`

### 2. `ConfigureHttpMessageHandlerBuilder` obsoleted ([CS0618](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/compatibility/networking/9.0/obsolete-apis))
This API is marked `[Obsolete]` in .NET 9 and will not compile with `TreatWarningsAsErrors`.

**Before:** `ConfigureHttpMessageHandlerBuilder(b => { ((HttpClientHandler)b.PrimaryHandler).UseCookies = false; })`
**After:** `.ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler(() => new HttpClientHandler { UseCookies = false })`

### 3. Reverse-proxy headers — behavioral change
`ForwardedHeadersOptions` now **defaults `ForwardLimit` to `1`** (unchanged from .NET 8, but worth verifying). If you have multiple proxies, set `ForwardLimit` and add entries to `KnownProxies`/`KnownNetworks`.

### 4. Trace-level HTTP header logging — redacted by default
In .NET 9, Kestrel and `HttpClient` **redact header values** in trace logs. Headers you previously saw in full now show `[Redacted]`. To restore the old behavior, configure `HttpClientHandler` logging or set `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Logging.Content` to include specific headers.

### 5. `dotnet watch` — no longer restarts on rude edits
In .NET 9, `dotnet watch` **defaults to no-restart** when hot reload can't apply a change. Add `--restart` explicitly: `dotnet watch --restart run`.
